note: Fuzz harness entry: the raw input bytes are accepted as a TLS server handshake stream for the client fuzzer.
The client processes the server handshake messages (ServerHello, ServerKeyExchange, ServerHelloDone) fed via the input buffer.
The DH object parsed from the ServerKeyExchange is assigned to peer_tmp; ownership of dh transfers to peer_tmp.
The 512-bit DH prime yields security bits < 80, so ssl_security returns 0 at SECLEVEL=0 and control jumps to the err: label, violating the invariant that the DH object must not be freed twice.
invariant: DH object must not be freed more than once after ownership transfer to peer_tmp

note: In the err: path, DH_free(dh) is called even though dh was already assigned to peer_tmp, decrementing the reference count of an object that will be freed again by EVP_PKEY_free(peer_tmp).
EVP_PKEY_free(peer_tmp) frees the EVP_PKEY which still owns the same DH object, invoking DH_free a second time on already-freed memory.
Second DH_free on the same DH object performs CRYPTO_DOWN_REF on freed memory, causing the heap-use-after-free WRITE 4 reported in the crash state.
